plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial with large, fragrant, often double blooms atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed dark green leaves. A classic cottage garden favorite that returns reliably for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 50 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest cultivated roses, a compact, suckering shrub with richly scented, semi-double flowers in deep shades and bright golden stamens. It forms thickets and is the ancestor of many garden roses.
plants.location: Southern and Central Europe east to western Asia; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis', the Apothecary's Rose, was used medicinally for centuries and its petals retain fragrance when dried.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray, narrow foliage and slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers that attract bees and butterflies. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid summer (June to August) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning to wash, as the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spreading tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In bloom it carpets streets and gardens with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); September to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in subtropical regions including California, Mexico, South Africa, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas line the streets, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.
